From: Anna Patel <anna@brightgrid.com>

Date: 2026-08-25T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Volume discount on hosted API (BrightGrid)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightGrid is excited about the latency profile and the KV cache savings you showed. Before we move to procurement, our finance team asked for a clear proposal for per-token pricing tied to committed monthly spend.

Our expected usage profile: 60M generation tokens / month (95% text-gen, 5% embeddings) for the next 12 months, with spikes to 90M in Q4. We can commit to a minimum monthly spend if we get a stepped per-token band (i.e., lower price after 50M, lower again after 100M).

Can you share: 1) your rate card baseline for hosted API (per-gen token / per-embed unit), 2) a commit-tier proposal (volume breakpoints + committed USD/month), and 3) any approval path for custom price exceptions if the suggested tiers deviate from your published bands?

Also attaching our procurement template for reference.

Thanks,
Anna Patel
Head of Procurement, BrightGrid
procurement@brightgrid.com
Attachment: BrightGrid_MA_v1.pdf (PDF stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Volume discount on hosted API (BrightGrid)

Anna — really appreciate the clear numbers. Quick summary from our side and an ask to align expectations: 

- Baseline rate card (hosted API): $0.00035 per generation token; $0.0010 per embedding unit.
- Typical volume breakpoints we publish: 0-10M, 10M-50M, 50M-200M. Published discounts get more aggressive past 50M.

Given BrightGrid's profile (60M steady), I can propose an internal exception path: a committed tier at $0.00025/gen-token for usage between 50M-100M, with an overage rate of $0.00030 after that, conditioned on a 12-month minimum commitment and monthly reporting. Embeddings would move to $0.00085/unit above 50k/month.

Two asks: 1) Would BrightGrid accept a 30-day onboarding credit and a clause to review rates if monthly usage materially exceeds the commit (we'd want to avoid open-ended Q4 spikes without sync)? 2) Please confirm procurement's preferred contracting timeline so I can escalate to finance/legal for a formal exception.

I attached a quick calc (proposed_discount_calc.xlsx) to illustrate monthly cost at 60M vs 90M usage.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_discount_calc.xlsx (XLSX stub)

Subject: Fwd: BrightGrid volume pricing — request for approval (internal)

Team — forwarding BrightGrid's ask and my proposed exception. TL;DR: request approval to offer BrightGrid a committed tier: $0.00025/gen-token for 50–100M, $0.00030/gen-token over 100M; embeddings $0.00085/unit >50k. 12-month commit; monthly reporting; onboarding credit 1 month.

Why approve? Strategic account (SaaS platform with enterprise customers), predictable consumption, potential Dedicated later. Risk: Q4 spike exposure — propose a hard-cap review and auto-fallback to published rate if usage permanently exceeds 150% of commit for two consecutive months.

Please weigh in: quick approvals needed to meet their procurement timeline (they asked for contract draft by Aug 29).
